answer.rationale: The write-path latency degradation began shortly after a release, making rollback the most targeted intervention with historical precedent (memory_b1) of clearing a similar error spike without customer impact. Regional failover is explicitly contraindicated here because memory_b2 shows it caused write loss and replication gaps specifically when writes were hot, which is exactly the current condition (peak settlement traffic, heavy writes) — so that option is ruled out rather than chosen. I verify memory_b1 to confirm the rollback precedent was truly clean and not confounded by other factors, and memory_b2 to confirm the hot-writes failure mode is real and applicable now, since acting against it during peak settlement traffic could cause irreversible financial/customer harm. Add_capacity or circuit breakers don't address a release-correlated regression directly, and read-replica routing doesn't touch write-path latency. Given only one intervention is possible and peak writes are in flight, I'll proceed as a standard monitored rollback rather than a broad simultaneous multi-system change, watching for the write-loss failure mode noted in b2 even though this is a different mechanism (release revert vs. traffic shift).
